A public view getter pricePerShare() reads totalAssets/totalShares, so during the call's re-entrancy window an external reader observes ETH already sent but supply not yet reduced — inflated price-per-share. why_labeled: The 2a trigger genuinely matches (guard removed, external call remains, state written after the call), and the inconsistent view makes read-only reentrancy plausible. But exclusion 2.10 caps this at CANDIDATE: a single-repo tool cannot prove that a THIRD-PARTY protocol actually reads pricePerShare() inside the re-entrancy window, which is what turns read-only reentrancy from theoretical to exploitable. Per RULES.md the rule must downgrade to CANDIDATE and must NOT auto-confirm this as a positive. The `label` is 'candidate' so this fixture documents the intended verdict ceiling; the future detector will emit CANDIDATE here, never CONFIRMED.
